A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same generator-augmented-flow research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-generation experiments, coupling diagnostics, and ablations, including Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–9.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds ECT results on FFHQ and conditional ImageNet in Table 2.

M1.justification: The GC construction, consistency loss, frozen-predictor strategy, and joint IC/GC training remain unchanged, including Equations (13)–(15), Equation (21), and Algorithm 1. The additional benchmarks do not introduce a documented method modification.

E1.justification: Table 2 expands ECT evaluation from CIFAR-10 to FFHQ 64×64 and conditional ImageNet 64×64. The latter introduces explicitly conditional generation beyond v3's unconditional ImageNet-32 evaluation. All original dataset coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding iCT comparisons retain IC and minibatch-OT baselines, and Table 2 retains ECT-IC against ECT-GC. Extending this same comparison to additional datasets does not change comparator membership. The newly cited Lee et al. method is not evaluated.

E3.justification: No revision is reported to existing metrics, schedules, hyperparameters, or evaluation procedures. The additional Table 2 benchmarks retain the short/long ECT comparison design. Specifying short training as 4k iterations adds documentation rather than establishing a changed budget for the existing experiment.

E4.justification: The predictor-quality, coupling-discrepancy, transport-cost, joint-learning-factor, pure-GC failure, equal-time, dropout, and EMA analyses are retained. Appendix C and its ablation results are unchanged; the added Table 2 entries extend benchmark evaluation.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same uncertainty presentation and Appendix D's description of five evaluation resamplings from the same trained model for Table 1. The additional Table 2 rows use the existing ± presentation without introducing new run-count, interval-construction, or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds substantial ECT evidence with mixed outcomes. FFHQ favors GC at 4k iterations (FID 11.73 versus IC's 13.29) and 100k (8.51 versus 9.68). Conditional ImageNet favors GC at 4k (10.31 versus 10.82), but IC at 100k (5.84 versus GC's 6.39). Existing CIFAR-10 scores, Tables 1 and 3, and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.4 derives a Jacobian singular-value bound connecting the quadratic discrepancy term to its proxy, plus an equality under a scaling-model assumption, in Equations (91)–(92). Appendix A.1 adds mathematical arguments about the scaling and regularity restrictions of prior equivalence results. The existing theorems and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the CT/CD discrepancy, generator-augmented flows, reduced proxy discrepancy and transport cost, and improved training. Additional evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a conditional justification for interpreting the proxy as controlling the actual discrepancy through quadratic-loss and Jacobian assumptions. Existing explanations of pure-GC failure remain unchanged. The new long-training conditional ImageNet result favoring IC receives no corresponding discussion.

D1.justification: Table 2 newly specifies 4,000 iterations for short ECT training, previously described only as approximately one GPU-hour. Implementation descriptions, hardware, hyperparameter tables, and code-access statements otherwise remain unchanged; detailed setups for the added benchmarks are not supplied.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds Lee et al. (2023) and its encoder-based data–noise coupling approach. Appendix A.1 expands the explanation of how this work relates to Song et al. (2023)'s equivalence theorems. The broader positioning against independent coupling and OT remains intact.

P1.justification: There are localized wording and notation corrections, additional appendix explanations and cross-references, and new affiliation, publication, and acknowledgement text. The main section order and overall narrative are preserved.

P2.justification: Table 2 is expanded into dataset-and-budget groups, with a revised caption and FID direction marker. Figure 1's caption is lightly revised. Existing graphics are retained, while Algorithm 1 and several appendix displays shift placement within the same overall layout.

improvement.justification: v4 provides more informative evidence about ECT generalization, including an unfavorable case, and clarifies the proxy's mathematical justification and relationship to prior theory. These are useful, limited gains. Their value is tempered by sparse setup documentation for the added benchmarks and retained prose in Section 5.3 and Appendix D that does not address the conditional ImageNet exception.
